tour.name: Ninh Binh Private Day Trip from Hanoi: Trang An Boat, Hoa Lu Ancient Capital & Mua Cave
tour.subtitle: A private day in 'Ha Long Bay on land' with a licensed guide and car: the temples of Hoa Lu, Vietnam's 10th-century capital, a rowing boat through the caves and karst valleys of Trang An, a cycle through the rice fields and the climb to the dragon on top of Mua Cave.

tour.overview:
Two hours south of Hanoi, the Red River delta meets a forest of limestone towers. Rivers wind between them through flooded caves, and rice fields fill the valleys, turning green in spring and gold in early summer. In 968 the first emperor of an independent Vietnam, Dinh Bo Linh, chose this natural fortress for his capital, Hoa Lu. The Trang An Landscape Complex, combining nature, archaeology and history, has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2014.

This private day takes you through Ninh Binh with a licensed guide and a car. You visit the temples of Hoa Lu, glide through the caves of Trang An in a sampan rowed by a local, have lunch, cycle along the rice fields and climb to the viewpoint of Mua Cave for the most famous view of the region.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 11 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Hanoi
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver, sampan and bicycles
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; about 500 steep steps at Mua Cave (optional)

WHAT YOU SEE
• The temples of the Dinh and Le kings at Hoa Lu.
• The Trang An boat route, its caves and temples.
• The rice fields of Tam Coc by bicycle.
• Mua Cave and its viewpoint.

WHY THIS WORKS
We reach Trang An before the midday crowds and climb Mua Cave in the late afternoon, when the light over the valley is best.

WHO IT SUITS
Nature lovers, photographers and active families.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer the sea, choose our Ha Long Bay day cruise.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The rice is green from February to April and golden from late May to early June, then again in September and October. The Trang An boat trip lasts about two to three hours, with low caves where you must duck.

days.name: Hoa Lu, the Trang An boat trip, lunch, cycling in Tam Coc and the Mua Cave viewpoint
days.description:
What to expect: the karst landscapes and ancient capital of Ninh Binh, with a licensed guide, private car, boat, bicycles, tickets and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 7:30 for the drive south, about two hours. At Hoa Lu, enclosed by limestone hills that formed its walls, you visit the temples of King Dinh Tien Hoang, who unified the country in 968, and King Le Dai Hanh, his successor, with their carved stone dragons, lacquered altars and courtyards shaded by old trees. Your guide tells the story of the first independent Vietnamese dynasties and why the capital later moved to Hanoi.

At Trang An you board a sampan, a small flat boat rowed by a local woman or man, often with their feet. For about two and a half hours you glide along rivers between towering cliffs, through a series of caves – some so low you lie back to pass under the rock – and stop at small temples on islands, including the reconstructed set built here for the film Kong: Skull Island. The only sounds are the oars and the birds.

Lunch features Ninh Binh's specialities: goat meat, with lemongrass or ginger, and com chay, crispy rice cakes with a savoury topping. In the afternoon you cycle along quiet lanes through the rice fields of Tam Coc, past water buffaloes and villages, then reach Mua Cave. From the foot of the hill, about 500 steep stone steps climb to a summit crowned with a stone dragon, with a view over the Ngo Dong river winding between rice fields and karst peaks – the most photographed panorama of northern Vietnam. You drive back to Hanoi, arriving at about 18:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:30 – Pick-up at your hotel in Hanoi.
09:30 – Hoa Lu ancient capital.
10:30 – Trang An boat trip (about 2 hours 30 minutes).
13:15 – Lunch.
14:30 – Cycling in Tam Coc.
15:30 – Mua Cave viewpoint.
16:30 – Drive back to Hanoi.
18:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Bai Dinh pagoda, one of the largest Buddhist complexes in Vietnam, can replace Hoa Lu.
• A night in a homestay among the rice fields can be added.
• The boat has no shade: bring a hat and sun cream; umbrellas are provided.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, tickets and boat, bicycles, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks with lunch, tips for the rower.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is the boat trip private?
faq.answer: Each sampan carries up to four passengers with its rower; your group has its own boats.

faq.question: Do we have to climb Mua Cave?
faq.answer: No. The 500 steps are steep and optional; there is a pleasant garden and lotus pond at the bottom.

faq.question: Are the tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: Hoa Lu, the Trang An boat and Mua Cave, plus bicycles and lunch.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, with Ninh Binh's specialities. Vegetarian and other diets are easy to arrange.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the caves and the cycling; child seats on bikes and in the car are available.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The boat needs a step down, and Mua Cave is steep. Hoa Lu and the boat trip itself are easy.

faq.question: Can we skip the cycling?
faq.answer: Yes. We can drive through the rice fields instead, or replace the ride with a second boat trip at Tam Coc.

faq.question: When is the rice golden?
faq.answer: Usually from late May to early June, and again in September and October. In spring the fields are bright green.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Vietnam, especially for the boat rowers, but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes, a hat, sun cream, comfortable shoes and covering clothes for the temples.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: February to June and September to November. Summer is hot and rainy; winter is cool and sometimes grey.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
